module_title: Principles of Insurance and Key Terminology
introduction: Insurance contracts are bound by highly specific legal principles. If these principles are violated by the customer, the insurance company has the legal right to reject the claim.

core_concepts.title: Principle of Utmost Good Faith (Uberrimae Fidei)
core_concepts.description: This means both parties must be entirely transparent. When buying a policy, you must disclose all 'material facts' truthfully (e.g., pre-existing diseases, smoking habits). Hiding facts makes the contract void.

core_concepts.title: Principle of Insurable Interest
core_concepts.description: You can only buy insurance for something whose destruction would cause you a direct 'financial loss'. (You can insure your own car, but you cannot legally insure your neighbor's car because its damage doesn't hurt you financially).

core_concepts.title: Principle of Indemnity
core_concepts.description: Applicable only to General Insurance. It means insurance is designed to put you back in the exact financial position you were in 'before' the loss occurred. You cannot make a 'profit' out of an insurance claim. (Note: This does NOT apply to Life Insurance, as human life cannot be valued in money).

core_concepts.title: Reinsurance
core_concepts.description: When an insurance company feels it has taken on too much risk, it passes a portion of that risk (and the premium) to another, larger insurance company. It is basically 'insurance for insurance companies'.

important_entities.name: Insurance Ombudsman
important_entities.significance: If an insurance company wrongly rejects your claim or harasses you, you can file a complaint with the Insurance Ombudsman. It acts as a free, out-of-court settlement mechanism for policyholders.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often mistakenly group Health Insurance under Life Insurance because it deals with the human body. Technically, Health Insurance falls strictly under 'General Insurance' (or Standalone Health) because it reimburses actual hospital expenses (Indemnity).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Utmost Good Faith (Truth), Insurable Interest (Your loss), Indemnity (No profit).

exam_strategy_tips: What is the current FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) limit in the Indian Insurance Sector? Answer: 74% under the automatic route. This is a highly repeated current affairs and static GK question.
